I never went to school. Everything I know about farming I learned from my mother and from doing it myself for 35 years. My farm is 10.1 mu. I keep 7 mu for wheat and maize — wheat in the fall, then maize right after we cut the wheat in June. The other 3.1 mu I plant with cotton. My husband works in the city now, so it is mostly me, but I hire my nephew for harvest and cotton picking.

For the wheat, I do what I did last year because it worked. I buy the improved seed from the township shop — about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing in October, I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, that is 100 jin. In March when the wheat starts growing fast, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 50 jin. Auntie Li next door does the same and her wheat always looks good. I irrigate three times: once in winter if the ground is too dry, once when the wheat shoots up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — herbicide first, then insecticide. I use the rotary tiller before planting. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, this year I hope for the same if the weather holds.

For the maize, we plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There is no time to plow deep, so we use no-tillage and the seed drill. I put down compound fertilizer in the rows when planting — about half a bag per mu — and spread some urea later when the plants are knee-high, about 40 jin per mu. Not as much as wheat because summer rain helps. I irrigate twice if the rain is not enough. Two sprays is enough for maize bugs. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

For cotton, it needs more care and more sprays. I rotary till in April. I plant hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. Cotton needs the fertilizer with more potassium, so I buy the special compound fertilizer from the dealer — the one in the red bag. I put almost one bag per mu, and a little urea when it flowers. I irrigate twice and spray four times because the bollworm always comes. Last year cotton gave me about 600 jin per mu. I do not dare to cut back on fertilizer — wasting some money on extra fertilizer is better than a bad harvest. A bad harvest means no money for my husband's medicine and no savings for the year.
